newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE- MARCH 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE- MARCH 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--A new battle front has been established between the government and unions following the revelations of changes planned by the government to labour relations. Objections have come from the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) as well as members of ruling PASOK while employers' groups have been positive in their reactions.
--Steps towards cheaper loans and new lending products are being taken surely but gradually following the Bank of greece's intervention in the interbank market.
--On the basis of current figures, average dividends for 38 listed ASE members have increased 5.0 percent.

--The Bank of Greece's dramatic reduction of interest rates in the interbank market by 2.0 points will probably force banks to new rate reductions in lending and deposits within the week. Banking circles say the rate cuts are expected to reduce the cost of money for banks.

--The environment, town planning and public works ministry is expected to put up 60 billion drachmas worth of public works projects in what sources say is a concerted attempt to unblock delays due to red tape.
--Wage increases to workers in public utilities and organisations (DEKOs) will not exceede 5.0 percent as the government is determined to defend its incomes policy throughout the public sector.
--The Athen Stock Exchange's performance in the first three months of the year has created news conditions on the market and hopes for an improvement in the climate on the bourse.

--The government is determined to stand firm in the face of demands by workers in DEKOs and banks for wage increased exceeding targets foreseen in the government's income policy. Both the prime minister and the national economy and finance minister have warned the administrations that they will pay the cost of granting increases above the targets, which cannot exceed 7.0 percent.

--Eight labour ministry proposals look set to change the face of labour relations and employment in Greece: based on announcements by the prime minister during his meetieng last week with ruling PASOK-aligned unionists, the proposals will be put o the table during social dialogue. They include changes to work hours, part-time employmnet, bargaining agreements and the reduction of non-wage labour costs such as pension contributions.

--Jostling for a share of the banking market continues unabated as each bank drafts its own strategy to increase its market share and influence. Alpha Credit Bank is investing in its network but not prepared to squander money and time on banks with small market shares, while third-largest private bank Eurobank has increased its influence with its purchase of Credti Lyonnais domestic retail network.

--The Athens bourse swings upwards again as Friday's session showed an increase in the general prixce index of 3.3 percent. Capital outflows from the interbank market were restricted to 100 billion drachmas, indicating that the markets considers the margins for deceleration of interest rates is a given. Yet another international investment house - Carnegie - issued another positive report on the Greek economy, further boosting confidence in the market.
